# What Cloudflare Origin CA keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is. The run written once and eight characters of it again is the
# twenty-four of the first run; written nine times and two characters more it is
# the hundred and forty-six of the second; and with the prefix and the separator
# between them that comes to the hundred and seventy-six characters Cloudflare's
# own format is written to. The counts are not an abbreviation — a run shortened
# for readability would leave a case holding no key at all. The body is
# hexadecimal and lowercase, so the run repeats those sixteen characters rather
# than carrying on through the alphabet, and the case that turns on case is
# written with the same run in uppercase.

patterns: cloudflare-origin-ca-key

# A key as it is written. Cloudflare issues one under this name, sends it as a
# header of its own rather than in a bearer header, and reads it from the Origin
# CA certificates API and from the Keyless SSL key server. So what is below
# differs in where a key stands rather than in what it is.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_CA_KEY=v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_CA_KEY=«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     a key in the service key header
in:       X-Auth-User-Service-Key: v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      X-Auth-User-Service-Key: «cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "X-Auth-User-Service-Key: v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01" https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/certificates
out:      curl -H "X-Auth-User-Service-Key: «cloudflare-origin-ca-key»" https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/certificates

case:     a key in a json body
in:       {"service_key":"v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01"}
out:      {"service_key":"«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»"}

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01.
out:      the key is «cloudflare-origin-ca-key».

case:     a key flush against a multi-byte rune on both sides
in:       日本語v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01日本語
out:      日本語«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»日本語

case:     a key in a tab separated field
in:       origin_ca_key\tv1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      origin_ca_key\t«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     a key followed by a crlf
in:       CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_CA_KEY=v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01\r\n
out:      CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_CA_KEY=«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»\r\n

case:     a key in a markdown code span
in:       `v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01`
out:      `«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»`

# The alphabet, which is one class over both runs: lowercase hexadecimal. It is
# read in lowercase alone, which the pattern's own file weighs — the whole of
# the body being one class, admitting the other case would draw in every
# uppercase hexadecimal run written behind a version string and buy no key a
# narrower reading loses. The first case below writes the last letter of the
# class at the first and the last character of either run, which the ordered run
# reaches at neither end.

case:     both runs opening and closing on the last letter of the alphabet
in:       v1.0-f123456789abcdef0123456f-f123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0f
out:      «cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     an uppercase body
in:       v1.0-0123456789ABCDEF01234567-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01
out:      v1.0-0123456789ABCDEF01234567-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01

# The lengths. Cloudflare states neither of them: what states them is the whole
# value its API reference writes behind the header, corroborated by the two
# published rulesets that spell the same split and by a third that spells the
# width of the two runs and the separator together. Both are read as counts and
# not as floors, which cuts both ways: a run one character short is located
# nowhere, and a run one character longer is a key with a character written
# after it.

case:     a first run one character short
in:       v1.0-0123456789abcdef0123456-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      v1.0-0123456789abcdef0123456-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a second run one character longer is a key and the character after it
in:       v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef010
out:      «cloudflare-origin-ca-key»0

# The separator, which stands at the twenty-fifth character behind the prefix
# and at no other, and is the one character of a body that is no hexadecimal
# digit. The two runs written against each other put nothing where it belongs,
# and the reading ends at that character.

case:     the two runs written with no separator between them
in:       v1.0-0123456789abcdef012345670123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      v1.0-0123456789abcdef012345670123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever word character it abuts, and what
# stands past the hundred and seventy-sixth character stays where it was
# written. The first two cases are what a boundary in front would cost; the
# third is what it would buy, which is a word closing on the character a key
# opens with.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_CA_KEY_v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_CA_KEY_«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xv1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      x«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     a word closing on the character a key opens with
in:       rev1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      re«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01suffix
out:      «cloudflare-origin-ca-key»suffix

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01-suffix
out:      «cloudflare-origin-ca-key»-suffix

# Two keys written together, and a key written inside a candidate. The character
# a key opens with is written in neither run and nowhere else in the prefix, so
# it stands once in a key and a second key can begin at no character of the
# first — the two redactions below meet rather than overlap. The scan advances
# rather than consuming its match all the same, and what that finds is the key
# standing inside a candidate that is no key.

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef23
out:      «cloudflare-origin-ca-key»«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

case:     a candidate whose body opens with a prefix
in:       v1.0-v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      v1.0-«cloudflare-origin-ca-key»

# The prefix as ordinary text writes it: v1.0- is how a pre-release version is
# written. What turns those away is the body rather than the prefix, and on a
# line of their own it is the count that does it: none of the three carries
# anywhere near the hundred and seventy-one characters a key has behind its
# prefix.

case:     a pre-release version
in:       v1.0-beta
out:      v1.0-beta

case:     a release candidate
in:       v1.0-rc1
out:      v1.0-rc1

case:     the output of git describe
in:       v1.0-12-g0123abc
out:      v1.0-12-g0123abc

# And what this pattern leaves alone otherwise. A body of the right shape with
# no prefix in front of it, a digest written where the second run stands — no
# digest is written to either count, an MD5 being thirty-two characters, a SHA-1
# forty, a SHA-256 sixty-four and a SHA-512 a hundred and twenty-eight — and the
# log line no pattern here has anything to find in.

case:     a body of the right shape opening with no prefix
in:       x1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      x1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a sha256 where the second run stands
in:       v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      v1.0-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/certificates
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/certificates
